title: Other old bass and tuba players: John Porter and Frank Robinson
summary: Breaux and the interviewer try to place John Porter and Frank Robinson, who played tuba with a band that rehearsed on St. Peter Street.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: I don't know. No, well, uh, old man, uh, I knew those fellas were good. Mr. John Porter was a good bass, too, a player.

I didn't know him too well, but I know Mr. John Porter is a player. He was. This other old man used to be with the Tonic Tribe, used to play a nice bass tuba too. And that's the same man you're talking about. Used to be along with Mr. Pritchett and them?
I just remember his name. I'll ask Red Gloff.
Was that when Red Gloff was playing trombone with him? He was with that man, I think. I think Frank was around during that time.

Maybe that's the same fella I'm talking about. I know he played a nice bass and he used to read well because, uh, I used to rehearse with him a couple of times. Yeah, well, I started playing with him right down St. Peter Street where the Tonic Tribe used
to rehearse him. Because Ed, Ed, Ed, Ed, it takes some lessons, bass lessons from him.

He was a cook. Right, St. Peter between Liberty and Murray. He started a school there. Mr. Jones, the one with the Jones home? Yeah, yeah. He started a school there. And, uh, well, that's a long time ago. I mean, I was a kid there.
I was in school and stuff
